premise.reason: The §9 slice is a go/no-go smoke gate: four arms (the W1 assembly plus the C0/C0b/C1 controls), run BEFORE the million-ball budget is spent, to decide whether H6 is worth pursuing. Its TIMEOUT tail earns the same exemption as A1/A2/B, with one of the three supporting measurements necessarily substituted, and the substitution is stated rather than glossed. (1) The timeouts are observed outcomes, not censored ones, and this is the cleanest case of the four: re-running the slice at a 12.0s cap instead of 4.0s leaves cp at 0.08917 - IDENTICAL to five decimal places - while TIMEOUT falls 33.20% to 10.35%. Tripling the window converts not one timeout into a catch; the balls that stop timing out settle somewhere that is not the pocket. (2) SUBSTITUTED. The other stages argue that the tail sits in the rows they reject; the slice has no top-N to be outside of, so that argument is unavailable and is not being pretended to. What replaces it is what the slice is FOR: it does not rank anything, it compares. The tail is present in every arm (C0 52.87%, C1 39.00%, W1 40.67%, C0b 0.27%), and cp is 0.00% in BOTH no-wall controls against 35.67% for W1. A timeout suppresses cp - it can never manufacture a catch - so the tail can only understate W1's margin, never create it. The go/no-go decision cannot be flipped by it in the direction that matters, and the window-extension check in (1) confirms the margin does not move when the tail is given three times as long to resolve. (3) Solver validity is clean: IMPACTS_EXHAUSTED, ESCAPED and NAN are all ZERO. Measured 33.200% flagged excluding STALLED, all of it TIMEOUT. Ceiling set at 38% as a bound with headroom, not as a measurement.
